title: Playing the Harlemites records and identifying soloists
summary: Collier plays 'Sweet Madness' and 'Harlem Bound' with the personnel list, and Briggs identifies Billy Burns and Herb Fleming as the trombone soloists.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: We're going to pause here now, because there are two more records with the Harlemites, that Mr. Briggs would like to get included on this oral history.
These are "Sweet Madness" and "Harlem Bound" played by Freddie Johnson and

his Harlemites. And the band includes Arthur Briggs, and Bobby Jones on trumpets; Billy Burns and Herb Fleming on trombones; Booker Pittman, clarinet and alto; Clay Sandler, alto; Roy Butler, alto, baritone; Alfred Pratt, tenor; Freddy Johnson, piano, arranger; Sterling Conaway, guitar; Juan Fernandez, bass; Billy Taylor, drums. And it was recorded in Paris, around October, 1933.
(A musical recording of the Harlemites was played at this time.)
This is the number 5 tape, Arthur Briggs interview, February 26, 1982.
We were interrupted on "Harlem Bound" record which was recorded in Paris in October of 1933 by Freddie Johnson and his Harlemites.
We will now go back and pick that record up again.

Mr. Briggs identifies the trombone player on "Harlem Bound" as Billy Burns. That's a solo that comes in on the last third of the record. And then the solo on the previous record, "Sweet Madness", that was Herb Fleming.
